title: Venison Stew with Juniper and Red Wine
subtitle: Rich, slow-cooked venison with woodland aromatics
excerpt: Venison shoulder braised low and slow in red wine with juniper, thyme, and root vegetables until the meat is fall-apart tender and the sauce is dark and intensely flavoured. A winter stew of real depth.

recipe.sourceNotes: Venison has been a central feature of British cooking since medieval times, when it was reserved for the nobility and hunted across royal forests. The pairing of venison with juniper berries is traditional across northern Europe: the resinous, pine-like flavour of juniper complements the dark, slightly gamey flavour of the meat and is used in Scandinavian, German, and French game cooking as well as British. Modern farmed venison from red deer is lean, affordable, and widely available in supermarkets.

recipeTools.notes: Heavy casserole dish with a lid.

content.text: Venison is very lean and can dry out if cooked at too high a temperature. The oven should be at 150 C, no higher: low and slow gives tender, moist meat while a higher temperature can make even a long braise dry. Browning the meat in batches is non-negotiable: it adds colour and flavour to the whole stew. The red wine needs to be one you would drink, not cooking wine.

Pat the venison dry and season with salt and pepper. Heat the oil in a casserole over high heat. Brown the meat in batches for 3 to 4 minutes per batch without moving it. Remove each batch and set aside.
Reduce the heat to medium. Add the onion, carrot, and celery to the pan and cook for 8 minutes. Add the garlic and tomato puree and stir for 2 minutes. Sprinkle over the flour and stir through.

Add the red wine and let it bubble, scraping up any browned bits from the pan. Add the stock, juniper berries, thyme, bay leaves, and rosemary. Return the meat and any resting juices. Bring to a simmer.

Cover and transfer to an oven at 150 C / fan 130 C / gas 2. Cook for 2 to 2.5 hours until the venison is completely tender. Remove the herb sprigs. Taste and adjust seasoning. Serve with mashed potato or crusty bread.
